project.name: Train Ticket
project.description: Microservice-based train ticket booking system with 42 microservices covering user authentication, train travel search, order reservation & payment, food catering, admin management, and infrastructure support.

nodes.name: User Authentication
nodes.summary: Handles user identity registration, login authentication, JWT token issuance and validation, and captcha-based identity verification. Serves as the security gateway for all other microservices in the system.

businessRules: Passwords must be encoded with BCrypt before storage
JWT tokens must be validated on every authenticated request
Users must have unique usernames
All protected endpoints require a valid Authorization header
crossDomainInteractions: Provides JWT identity tokens consumed by all other services
User entities are referenced by order, food, and admin services
Auth service manages user lifecycle that impacts all downstream domains

nodes.name: Train Travel Search
nodes.summary: Manages the full catalog of train routes, station information, train types, seat availability, and travel schedules. Provides query APIs for searching direct and transfer routes, computing cheapest and quickest journey options, and planning multi-segment trips.

businessRules: High-speed rail (travel) and regular train (travel2) follow separate scheduling rules
Route planning must compute direct, transfer, cheapest, and quickest options
Seat availability must be checked before reservation
Station names are normalized to lowercase for consistency
crossDomainInteractions: Travel search results are the primary input for order reservation
Admin management services control route and travel CRUD operations
Route and station data is consumed by food catering for delivery zone matching

nodes.name: Order and Reservation Management
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the complete ticket purchasing lifecycle: reservation via message queue, order creation, price computation, payment processing (including account balance management), ticket cancellation with refund, rebooking to alternate trips, waitlist ordering, insurance purchase, luggage consignment, and final ticket execution.

businessRules: Reservation requests are queued via RabbitMQ for ordered processing
Order price must be computed before payment can proceed
Payment must deduct from user account balance before order is confirmed
Cancellation refund amount depends on timing relative to departure
Rebooking creates a new order and cancels the original
Waitlist orders activate in FIFO order when inventory becomes available
crossDomainInteractions: Reserves seats from the travel search domain
Requires authenticated user identity from user-authentication domain
Order status changes trigger notifications via infrastructure-support domain
Admin management domain provides order oversight and manual intervention capability

nodes.name: Food and Catering Services
nodes.summary: Manages the onboard and station food ordering experience: browsing train food menus and station food stores, placing food orders matched to specific trips and delivery stations, and orchestrating food delivery logistics through RabbitMQ-based messaging between food, delivery, and notification services.

businessRules: Food orders must be linked to a valid trip and seat
Station food delivery zone must match the order's delivery station
Food orders trigger asynchronous delivery workflow via RabbitMQ
Delivery status is tracked through the delivery lifecycle
crossDomainInteractions: Depends on travel search domain for trip, seat, and station data
Depends on order-management domain for valid ticket/trip context
Uses RabbitMQ for asynchronous communication with delivery service
Food order updates trigger notifications via infrastructure-support domain

nodes.name: Admin Management
nodes.summary: Provides administrative oversight of the entire system through REST APIs: managing user accounts, monitoring and modifying orders, maintaining route and travel catalogs, configuring pricing information, and controlling basic system settings. Serves as the backend powering the admin dashboard frontend.

businessRules: Admin operations require elevated privileges
Admin can view and modify all users' orders
Route and travel data created by admin feed the travel search catalog
Admin pricing config affects all order computations
crossDomainInteractions: Manages user accounts in user-authentication domain
Oversees and modifies orders in order-management domain
Controls route and travel data used by train-travel-search domain
Configures pricing that affects order-management domain

nodes.name: Infrastructure and Support Services
nodes.summary: Provides cross-cutting infrastructure capabilities: centralized configuration management for all microservices, email notification delivery for system events (order confirmations, cancellations, delivery updates), and ticket office operations. Acts as the operational backbone that keeps all business domains connected and informed.

businessRules: Configuration values are centrally managed and distributed
Notifications are triggered by domain events via RabbitMQ
Email notifications are composed and dispatched via SMTP
Ticket office provides offline/alternative ticket operations
crossDomainInteractions: Receives event messages from order-management and food-catering domains via RabbitMQ
Provides configuration values consumed by all other microservices
Dispatches email notifications for order, payment, and delivery events

nodes.name: User Registration
nodes.summary: Registers a new user account by validating input uniqueness, encoding the password, and persisting the user entity for subsequent authentication.

nodes.name: User Login
nodes.summary: Authenticates a user by verifying credentials against stored records and issues a signed JWT bearer token for accessing protected resources across all microservices.

nodes.name: Identity Verification
nodes.summary: Generates and validates captcha-based verification codes to confirm user identity during registration and sensitive operations, preventing automated abuse.

nodes.name: Token Management
nodes.summary: Intercepts every authenticated HTTP request to extract, validate, and refresh JWT tokens, establishing the security context used by downstream business logic.

nodes.name: Route Query
nodes.summary: Manages the full lifecycle of train route data: listing all available routes, fetching individual route details, creating new routes, updating existing routes, and deleting obsolete routes from the catalog.

nodes.name: Travel Search
nodes.summary: Searches for train travel options by querying trips based on route and departure date, returning detailed travel information including train type, station stops, and departure/arrival times.

nodes.name: Trip Planning
nodes.summary: Computes optimal journey options by searching for direct routes, transfer routes, the cheapest available itinerary, and the quickest travel path, aggregating results from multiple travel and route services.

nodes.name: Seat Management
nodes.summary: Queries real-time seat availability for specific trips, assigns seats to confirmed reservations, and releases seats back to the pool upon cancellation or expiration.

nodes.name: Ticket Reservation
nodes.summary: Processes a ticket reservation request by validating order data, checking seat availability, enqueueing the request through RabbitMQ for ordered processing, creating the reservation record, and triggering the payment flow.

nodes.name: Order Creation
nodes.summary: Creates a ticket order record after successful reservation, computing the final price based on route distance, train type, seat class, and any applicable insurance or consignment fees before persisting the order entity.

nodes.name: Payment Processing
nodes.summary: Processes ticket payment by querying the order amount, deducting from the user's account balance, recording the payment transaction, updating the order status to paid, and triggering ticket execution.

nodes.name: Order Cancellation
nodes.summary: Cancels a confirmed ticket order by looking up the current order status, computing the applicable refund amount (potentially with penalty based on timing), reversing the payment, releasing the reserved seat, and updating the order record to cancelled status.

nodes.name: Ticket Rebooking
nodes.summary: Rebooks an existing ticket to a different trip by validating eligibility, searching for alternative trips on the target date, computing the price difference, and creating an exchange order that replaces the original.

nodes.name: Food Menu Query
nodes.summary: Browses available food options by listing train food items for specific trains, station food stores at given stations, and food items available for delivery at planned trip stops.

nodes.name: Food Order Creation
nodes.summary: Places a food order by validating the order against the trip context, matching it to the correct delivery station, persisting the food order record, and sending an asynchronous notification to the delivery service via RabbitMQ.

nodes.name: Food Delivery
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the end-to-end food delivery process: receiving delivery notifications from the food service via RabbitMQ, assigning delivery routes matched to station stops, tracking delivery status through the fulfillment lifecycle, and marking orders as delivered.

nodes.name: Admin User Management
nodes.summary: Administers user accounts through privileged APIs: listing all registered users, creating new user accounts, modifying user profile information, and deleting user accounts from the system.

nodes.name: Admin Order Management
nodes.summary: Provides administrative oversight of all ticket orders: querying the complete order database, manually updating order statuses when needed, and removing invalid or test order records.

nodes.name: Admin Travel Management
nodes.summary: Manages the train travel catalog from the admin perspective: listing all travel entries, adding new travel schedules, updating travel details (routes, times, train types), and deleting travel records to keep the catalog current.

nodes.name: Admin Route Management
nodes.summary: Administers the train route catalog: listing all configured routes, creating new route definitions with station sequences and distances, updating route information, and removing deprecated routes.

nodes.name: Configuration Management
nodes.summary: Centrally manages system configuration values used by all microservices: querying current config entries, creating or updating configuration key-value pairs, and removing obsolete configuration entries.

nodes.name: Notification Delivery
nodes.summary: Processes outbound notifications triggered by system events: receiving event messages via RabbitMQ from order and delivery services, composing formatted email messages, dispatching emails through SMTP, and logging notification delivery results.

nodes.name: Validate Registration Input
nodes.summary: Validates that the username, password, and other required registration fields are present, non-empty, and meet format requirements before proceeding.

nodes.name: Check Duplicate Username
nodes.summary: Queries the user repository to verify that the requested username does not already exist, rejecting duplicate registrations.

nodes.name: Encode Password
nodes.summary: Encodes the plain-text password using BCrypt hashing before storage to ensure passwords are never stored in cleartext.

nodes.name: Persist User Entity
nodes.summary: Saves the validated and encoded user entity to the database through the UserRepository, making the account available for subsequent logins.

nodes.name: Authenticate Credentials
nodes.summary: Looks up the user by username and verifies the supplied password against the stored BCrypt hash using Spring Security's authentication manager.

nodes.name: Generate JWT Token
nodes.summary: Creates a signed JSON Web Token containing the authenticated user's identity, roles, and expiration time using the JWTProvider service.

nodes.name: Return Token and User Info
nodes.summary: Returns the generated JWT token along with basic user profile information (username, userId) in the login response to the client.

nodes.name: Generate Captcha Code
nodes.summary: Generates a random verification code (numeric or alphanumeric) and associates it with the requesting user's session or identifier for later validation.

nodes.name: Send Verification Code
nodes.summary: Delivers the generated verification code to the user through the configured channel (e.g., stored for later comparison or returned in a test/development environment).

nodes.name: Validate Verification Code
nodes.summary: Compares the user-submitted verification code against the previously generated and stored code, confirming identity if they match and are within the validity window.

nodes.name: Extract Token from Header
nodes.summary: Intercepts the incoming HTTP request and extracts the JWT bearer token from the Authorization header for validation.

nodes.name: Validate Token Signature
nodes.summary: Verifies the JWT token's cryptographic signature using the configured signing key to ensure the token was issued by this system and has not been tampered with.

nodes.name: Set Security Context
nodes.summary: Populates the Spring Security context with the authenticated user's principal and granted authorities, making the identity available to downstream controllers and services.

nodes.name: List All Routes
nodes.summary: Queries the RouteRepository to retrieve all configured train routes with their station sequences and returns them as a paginated or full list.

nodes.name: Get Route by ID
nodes.summary: Fetches detailed information for a single route identified by its route ID, including all intermediate stations, distances, and associated metadata.

nodes.name: Create or Update Route
nodes.summary: Accepts route definition data (station sequence, distances, route name) and either inserts a new route or modifies an existing one in the route catalog.

nodes.name: Delete Route
nodes.summary: Removes a route from the catalog by its route ID, ensuring no active trips reference the route before deletion.

nodes.name: Query Travel by Route and Date
nodes.summary: Searches the TripRepository for travel options matching a specified route and departure date, filtering results to only show trips with available seats.

nodes.name: Query Travel by Trip ID
nodes.summary: Fetches full travel details for a single trip identified by its unique TripId, including full station stop information and seat availability.

nodes.name: Return Travel Details
nodes.summary: Assembles the query results into a structured response containing trip information, train type, station stops with times, and available seat counts.

nodes.name: Search Direct Routes
nodes.summary: Queries travel services for trips that go directly from the origin station to the destination station without any transfers.

nodes.name: Search Transfer Routes
nodes.summary: Searches for multi-segment journeys requiring a transfer at an intermediate station, combining trip legs that together connect origin to destination.

nodes.name: Identify Cheapest Route
nodes.summary: Compares all found routes (direct and transfer) by total price, selecting the lowest-cost option from the search results.

nodes.name: Identify Quickest Route
nodes.summary: Compares all found routes by total travel duration, selecting the option with the shortest combined travel time.

nodes.name: Return Trip Plan Result
nodes.summary: Aggregates all computed route options (direct, transfer, cheapest, quickest) into a unified trip plan response returned to the client.

nodes.name: Query Seat Availability
nodes.summary: Checks the current seat inventory for a specified trip and travel date, returning the count and types of remaining available seats.

nodes.name: Assign Seat
nodes.summary: Reserves a specific seat (by seat number and class) for a confirmed order, decrementing the available seat count for the associated trip.

nodes.name: Release Seat
nodes.summary: Returns a previously assigned seat back to the available inventory when an order is cancelled or a reservation expires without payment.

nodes.name: Validate Reservation Request
nodes.summary: Validates the reservation request payload to ensure all required fields (trip ID, seat class, passenger info, contact details) are present and well-formed.

nodes.name: Check Seat Availability
nodes.summary: Calls the seat service to verify that the requested seat class still has availability on the specified trip before proceeding with the reservation.

nodes.name: Queue Reservation via RabbitMQ
nodes.summary: Publishes the validated reservation request to a RabbitMQ queue for ordered, asynchronous processing to prevent overselling under concurrent load.

nodes.name: Create Reservation Record
nodes.summary: Consumes the queued reservation message and persists a reservation record with status pending, linking it to the user, trip, and seat selection.

nodes.name: Invoke Payment Flow
nodes.summary: After successful reservation, triggers the payment processing flow by communicating the order amount and order ID to the payment service.

nodes.name: Validate Order Data
nodes.summary: Validates the order creation payload including passenger names, ID documents, contact info, and selected trip details.

nodes.name: Compute Order Price
nodes.summary: Calculates the total order price based on route distance, train type pricing, seat class multiplier, and any additional charges for insurance or consignment.

nodes.name: Persist Order Entity
nodes.summary: Saves the fully constructed order record with computed price and initial status to the OrderRepository for the primary or secondary order service.

nodes.name: Return Order Confirmation
nodes.summary: Returns the created order details including order ID, status, total price, and trip information as confirmation to the client.

nodes.name: Query Order Amount
nodes.summary: Retrieves the total payable amount for the order from the order service to determine how much to deduct from the user's account.

nodes.name: Deduct from Account
nodes.summary: Debits the order amount from the user's account balance, validating sufficient funds are available before the deduction proceeds.

nodes.name: Record Payment Transaction
nodes.summary: Persists a payment transaction record with the deducted amount, timestamp, order reference, and resulting account balance as an audit trail.

nodes.name: Update Order Status to Paid
nodes.summary: Updates the corresponding order's status from pending to paid upon successful payment, enabling subsequent ticket execution.

nodes.name: Issue Ticket Execution
nodes.summary: Triggers the execute service to finalize the ticket, generating the final ticket record with seat assignment and making it available to the passenger.

nodes.name: Lookup Order Status
nodes.summary: Retrieves the current order from the order repository to confirm it exists and is in a cancellable state (not already cancelled or executed beyond the refund window).

nodes.name: Compute Refund Amount
nodes.summary: Calculates the refund amount based on the order price, applying any cancellation penalty rules that depend on how far in advance of departure the cancellation occurs.

nodes.name: Reverse Payment
nodes.summary: Credits the computed refund amount back to the user's account balance, creating a reversal transaction record in the payment system.

nodes.name: Release Reserved Seat
nodes.summary: Calls the seat service to release the previously reserved seat back into the available inventory for the trip.

nodes.name: Update Order to Cancelled
nodes.summary: Updates the order status to cancelled and records the cancellation timestamp and refund amount in the order record.

nodes.name: Validate Rebook Eligibility
nodes.summary: Checks that the original order is in a paid/confirmed state, has not already been rebooked, and is within the allowed rebooking window before departure.

nodes.name: Search Alternative Trips
nodes.summary: Queries the travel search services for available trips on the desired new travel date matching the same route or a compatible alternative.

nodes.name: Compute Price Difference
nodes.summary: Calculates the price difference between the original ticket and the new trip, determining whether the user must pay additional amount or receive a partial refund.

nodes.name: Create Exchange Order
nodes.summary: Creates a new order for the replacement trip, links it to the original order for audit purposes, cancels the original order, and processes any net payment or refund.

nodes.name: List Train Food Items
nodes.summary: Queries the TrainFoodRepository for all food items available on a specific train, returning menu items with names, prices, and availability.

nodes.name: List Station Food Stores
nodes.summary: Queries the StationFoodRepository for food stores located at a given station, returning store names, food types, and operating hours.

nodes.name: Query Food by Trip
nodes.summary: Aggregates all food options (train food and station food) available for a specific trip, based on the trip's route and scheduled station stops.

nodes.name: Validate Food Order
nodes.summary: Validates the food order request: checks that the selected food items exist, quantities are positive, and the order is linked to a valid trip and seat.

nodes.name: Match Delivery Station
nodes.summary: Determines the optimal delivery station along the trip route where the food should be delivered, based on the food source and the trip's station stop schedule.

nodes.name: Persist Food Order
nodes.summary: Saves the validated food order to the FoodOrderRepository with status pending, linking it to the trip, seat, delivery station, and ordered items.

nodes.name: Notify Delivery Service
nodes.summary: Publishes a food delivery request message to RabbitMQ containing the order ID, delivery station, seat info, and trip details for the delivery service to process.

nodes.name: Receive Delivery Notification
nodes.summary: Listens on the RabbitMQ delivery queue and consumes incoming food delivery requests, extracting order and delivery details from the message payload.

nodes.name: Assign Delivery Route
nodes.summary: Plans the delivery logistics by assigning a delivery route matched to the trip's station stops, ensuring the food reaches the correct station at the right time.

nodes.name: Update Delivery Status
nodes.summary: Tracks the delivery through its lifecycle states (preparing, in-transit, delivered) by updating the FoodDeliveryOrder entity in the repository.

nodes.name: Mark Order Fulfilled
nodes.summary: Sets the final delivery status to fulfilled upon successful food delivery, completing the food order lifecycle.

nodes.name: List All Users
nodes.summary: Queries and returns a paginated list of all registered users with their profile details for administrative review.

nodes.name: Create New User
nodes.summary: Creates a new user account through the admin API with specified profile data, bypassing the standard registration flow.

nodes.name: Update User Profile
nodes.summary: Modifies an existing user's profile information including contact details and account settings through the admin interface.

nodes.name: Delete User Account
nodes.summary: Removes a user account from the system, handling cascading effects on associated orders and records.

nodes.name: Query All Orders
nodes.summary: Retrieves the complete order database across all users with filtering by status, date range, and other criteria for administrative oversight.

nodes.name: Update Order Status
nodes.summary: Manually modifies an order's status when manual intervention is required (e.g., resolving disputed payments, force-cancelling stuck orders).

nodes.name: Delete Order Record
nodes.summary: Removes an erroneous or test order record from the system, ensuring referential integrity with related payment and seat records.

nodes.name: Query All Travels
nodes.summary: Lists all travel entries in the system catalog with their associated routes, train types, departure times, and statuses.

nodes.name: Add New Travel
nodes.summary: Creates a new travel schedule entry by specifying route, train type, departure/arrival times, and other travel parameters.

nodes.name: Update Travel Information
nodes.summary: Modifies an existing travel entry's details such as departure time, train type assignment, or status.

nodes.name: Delete Travel Record
nodes.summary: Removes a travel entry from the catalog, ensuring no active orders reference the deleted travel.

nodes.name: List All Routes
nodes.summary: Retrieves all configured train routes with their station sequences and distances for administrative viewing.

nodes.name: Create Route
nodes.summary: Defines a new train route by specifying the ordered sequence of stations, station distances or travel times, and route metadata.

nodes.name: Update Route
nodes.summary: Modifies an existing route definition, adjusting station sequences, adding or removing stops, or updating distance/timing information.

nodes.name: Delete Route
nodes.summary: Removes a route definition from the system, ensuring no active travels or trips depend on the deleted route.

nodes.name: Query Configuration Values
nodes.summary: Retrieves all configuration entries or a specific configuration key from the centralized config repository.

nodes.name: Create or Update Config
nodes.summary: Inserts a new configuration key-value pair or updates an existing configuration entry with a new value.

nodes.name: Delete Config Entry
nodes.summary: Removes a configuration key and its value from the centralized config service when it is no longer needed.

nodes.name: Receive Notification Event
nodes.summary: Consumes event messages from the RabbitMQ notification queue triggered by order completions, cancellations, and delivery updates across the system.

nodes.name: Compose Email Message
nodes.summary: Formats the notification content into a structured email message with appropriate subject, body template, and recipient address derived from the event payload.

nodes.name: Dispatch via SMTP
nodes.summary: Sends the composed email notification through the configured SMTP mail service to the intended recipient.

nodes.name: Log Notification Result
nodes.summary: Records the notification delivery outcome (success, failure, bounced) in the NotifyRepository for audit and troubleshooting purposes.

edges.description: JWT tokens issued by auth service are required for all order, payment, and reservation endpoints; user identity flows from auth to order domain
Admin service manages user account lifecycle; user CRUD operations in admin domain directly affect auth domain user repository
Food orders require authenticated user identity from auth domain JWT token for order attribution
Travel search results, route data, and seat availability are primary inputs for ticket reservation and order creation flows
Trip, station, and seat information from travel domain is consumed by food catering to match delivery zones and validate food orders against valid trips
Confirmed ticket orders enable food ordering for the associated trip; food orders reference trip and seat from ticket orders
Order completion, cancellation, and payment events trigger email notifications dispatched by the notification service via RabbitMQ
Food delivery status changes trigger notification events sent through the infrastructure notification service
Admin oversight allows manual inspection and modification of all orders, including status override and record deletion
Admin creates and maintains route definitions and travel schedules that form the catalog consumed by the travel search domain
Configuration values from config service influence pricing and business rule parameters used by order and payment services
